lines.en: I walk to my stall with a hammer on my back.
My anvil sits behind the shop.
My apron is dusted with iron filings.
I walk the village path.
I step around the puddles.

lines.zh: 铺子里还挂着几件护甲。
lines.en: A few pieces of armor hang in the shop.
I walk over to check the furnace.
Clay clings to my boot soles.
My tool bag rides my shoulder.
I stop at the crossing and look around.
My hammer taps at my hip.
I make my way to that little house.
I sit on the doorstep to rest.
A little red still glows in the furnace.
I rest the hammer on my knee.
My hands are all callus.
I count today's trades.
The shop smells of iron.
I line the armor plates up neatly.
A butterfly net hangs by the door.
I'm waiting for a customer.
The wind swings the sign.
Iron prices are fair today.
I wipe the sweat from my brow.
A few coppers sit on the counter.
Have you come for armor?
I look up and size up your build.
That one's too worn; you need a new one.
I have a breastplate here.
Let me measure your shoulders first.
You don't smell of iron at all.
We don't take insect specimens here.
The one next door takes butterflies.
Would you like to see this one?
My prices are always fair.
That scar on your hand is old.
Sit a moment; I'll find it.
I've done this work many years.
Close the door behind you; it's drafty.
Don't touch that red-hot iron.
Let's discuss the price slowly.

lines.zh: 你要的东西我打得出来。
lines.en: I can hammer out what you need.
I retreat beside the anvil.
My arm has gone numb.
I can bind this myself.

lines.zh: 铁屑烫进伤口，我闷哼一声。
lines.en: Iron filings burn in the cut; I grunt once.
Blood drips onto the floor.
I'll need a moment after that.
The furnace still burns beside me.
I can still lift my hammer.
Now this is decent iron stock.
Are you trading this for armor?
Let me check the quality.
I can pay this much for it.
Do you have more scrap iron?
Put it on the counter; no rush.
Mediocre quality — not worth much.
This is enough for a pair of bracers.
One weigh in my hand and I'll know.
I'll take this piece of yours.
I'm heavier than I look.
You bumped the hammer on my shoulder.
I step back and steady the shelf.
Every plate in the shop rang.
There's a new footprint on the floor.
Don't crowd the counter.
You stepped on my apron.
Careful of that still-warm iron.
The shop keeps me busy.
Folk like me don't talk of that.
Just pass me the hammer.
Let's go into business together.
You hammer; I'll handle the coin.
Ask me once this rush is done.
These hands only know a hammer.
You're a craftsman too.
Then we're agreed.
We open as usual tomorrow.
This nail is still usable.
I pick it up and drop it in the bin.
Scrap iron — I'll keep it.
Your thing — I'll keep it safe.
I put it back on the shelf.
The quality really isn't good.
Whose is it? I'll leave it on the counter.
This is enough for one nail.
I tuck it into my apron pocket.
You've set the hammer down.
This isn't how a customer acts.

lines.zh: 铁匠看的是甲，不是蝴蝶。
lines.en: An armorer eyes armor, not butterflies.
I step back behind the counter.
The door is behind you.
I've shut the furnace door.
Next door will hear the noise.
My hammer comes to hand too.
I don't like hitting people.
I've put my bracers on.
There's nowhere to hide in here.

lines.zh: 我打得过铁，也打得过人。
lines.en: I can work iron, and I can hit.
I've moved beside the anvil.
Look — my hands are all callus.
Don't make me use force.
My hammer stays raised.
I kick the stool aside.
The anvil is at my right.
The shop is narrow; you can't dodge.
The bolt is behind me.

lines.zh: 你袖子里的东西，我看见了。
lines.en: I saw what's in your sleeve.
The furnace lights your face.
You've backed to the shelves.

lines.zh: 铁砧挡着我，我绕过去再说话。
lines.en: The anvil is in my way; I step around it to talk.

lines.zh: 这一下我会打你的手腕。
lines.en: I'll go for your wrist.
You've stepped on the iron filings.
Let's talk one more time.
Won't you just walk away?
One last question from me.
The hammer is already up.

lines.zh: 锤柄在我手里转了一圈。
lines.en: The hammer handle turns once in my grip.
I strike with the hammer's back.
That one caught your wrist.
My hammer is heavy.
I shove the anvil in front of you.
Whatever you held slipped free.
I didn't dare hit at full force.
You blocked it; your hand will go numb.
Iron filings scatter under our feet.
I've stepped back; don't follow.
That was only a warning.
Your armor can take it.
I turn the hammer crosswise.
Good that you can still stand.
The counter got knocked askew.
I push the shop door open.
The furnace fire has just caught.
There's dust on the anvil.
I hang my hammer on the wall.
The shop smells of new iron.
It isn't fully light outside.
I wipe down the counter.
Bracers are laid out in the window.
The net still hangs by the door.
A customer's footsteps approach.
I tie my apron tight.
Today will be busy from dawn to dusk.
I haul the iron stock inside.
The flame creeps up.
I lay my tools in a row.
Come in and have a look.
This shop has stood many years.
I draw the door curtain up.

lines.zh: 炉火把我的袖子燎着了。
lines.en: The furnace caught my sleeve.
I came down off the shelf.
Water has me coughing hard.

lines.zh: 气浪把我掀到柜台后面。
lines.en: The blast threw me behind the counter.
An arrowhead is stuck in my shoulder.

lines.zh: 那光把我手里的铁打冷了。
lines.en: That light chilled the iron in my hand.
A day without food and my hands shake.

lines.zh: 雷击把墙上的工具震落了。
lines.en: The strike shook the tools off the wall.
The floor beneath the shop is simply gone.
